newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cervecerias to build plant in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Cervecerias to build plant in Argentina.

text.p: Chile's largest brewery Cervecerias Unidas announced it will build a new $122 million plant in Argentina, where it already operates two brewing units, local media said Saturday.
The plant will be built within five years in Zarate, 40 miles north of Buenos Aires, CCU Argentina general manager Fernando Sanchis was quoted as saying.

CCU operates a plant in Santa Fe and Salta provinces, 500 and 800 miles north of Buenos Aires and has about an 8.0 percent of the Argentine beer market. In 1995, it launched a 10-year $250 million expansion plan to double output.
In Argentina, it produces Budweiser, the flagship brand of U.S. Anheuser Busch Cos Inc, under license and also has a PepsiCo bottling and distribution joint venture with Argentina's Baesa.
In Chile, it has a market share of nearly 90 percent. It also owns a controlling stake in one of the country's top wineries, Vina San Pedro.

CCU, controlled by Chilean group Luksic, also owns 67 percent of a Croatian brewery, Karlovacka Pivovara, and is looking into building a brewery in the Bosnian capital of Sarajevo, company officials have said. ((-- Guillermo Haskel, Buenos Aires Newsroom, 541 318-0650))
